operations.name: Frieda Zucker Katz

expected.name: Frieda Zucker Katz
expected.description: Frieda Zucker Katz was arrested in Cleveland on October 6, 1953 in the Ohio Smith Act roundup and held under $25,000 bail. After a fourteen-week trial, the jury acquitted Katz and three codefendants on February 10, 1956. The reviewed record does not establish a custodial interval after her arrest.

operations.name: Whirlwind Larson

expected.name: Whirlwind Larson
expected.description: Whirlwind Larson was a Chicago salesman for the Daily Worker and Sunday Worker who had immigrated to the United States in 1904. His attempts to obtain citizenship failed amid his labor activity and financial difficulties. After applying for permission to re-enter the country in 1934, he was summoned to a federal office, recognized as a labor-paper salesman, handcuffed and taken to the county jail for deportation proceedings. Larson was arrested at noon on a Thursday and freed at noon on Saturday after the International Labor Defense raised $1,000 cash bail. He then pledged to organize a neighborhood defense branch and raise money for other imprisoned workers.

operations.name: Torao Uyemura

expected.name: Torao Uyemura
expected.description: Torao Uyemura resisted conscription while confined at Heart Mountain, arguing that his citizenship rights had not been clarified. He pleaded not guilty to failing to report for a pre-induction physical, was convicted, and was imprisoned at McNeil Island in 1944.
